notes.text: Zach Hyman is out (impaired vision injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is a top-six forward. Connor McDavid has taken his spot beside Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and Kasperi Kapanen.
Kasperi Kapanen has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 54% of the team’s power-play time in 28 games, up from 6% last season.
Ty Emberson is no longer killing penalties: 4% of the team’s shorthanded time in 22 games, down from 30% last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 31% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 7th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 38%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Jared McCann is out 10 weeks (lower body injury) and has missed the last 12 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Kaapo Kakko has taken his spot beside Matty Beniers and Mackie Samoskevich. That line has had 76% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 55:01 together, up from 57% with McCann.

Cale Fleury has not dressed for the last 5 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Ryan Lindgren has taken his spot beside Josh Mahura. That pair has had 53% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 50:07 together.
Vince Dunn has started killing penalties: on the ice for 27% of the team’s shorthanded time in 23 games, up from 2% last season.

stakes: The Kraken go in tied for fourth in the Pacific with 25 points, 13 points behind the Oilers, first.

SEA.head: A slightly uphill night for the Kraken
SEA.body: Edmonton has been out-chancing opponents lately, but Seattle has home-ice advantage, and the Oilers will be without Hyman. The Kraken’s best way to tip it is keeping dangerous shots away.

EDM.head: Leaning the Oilers’ way
EDM.body: Edmonton has been out-chancing opponents lately, but Seattle has home-ice advantage, and the Oilers will be without Hyman. Still, it’s close: the Kraken can make it interesting if they keep dangerous shots away.

story.head: Draisaitl’s favorite opponent
paras: The teams have split two meetings this season. The Kraken are 12-10-1, while the Oilers are winless in five (0-4-1). This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Oilers first (third in the NHL) and the Kraken fourth (tied for 22nd). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.

The Oilers’ record (.679) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.548), largely thanks to their finishing. So is the Kraken’s (.543 on chances worth .442), largely thanks to their finishing.

The Oilers get their defensemen shooting (3rd). They also have one of the league’s most dangerous power plays (2nd), and that could do real damage against the Kraken’s penalty kill (30th). Edmonton has scored 3.75 goals a game, the third most in the league. On the other side, the Kraken rarely threaten on the penalty kill (32nd), give up a lot of shots (32nd) and ice the puck a lot (31st). The Kraken roll four lines, but the Oilers lean on their top six.

Connor McDavid (15 G / 45 A / 60 P in 28 GP) leads the Oilers and the whole NHL in scoring, with a point in five straight games against Seattle. Leon Draisaitl (24 G / 24 A / 48 P in 28 GP) has a team-high 24 goals, the most in the NHL. For the Kraken, Berkly Catton (8 G / 11 A / 19 P in 23 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Kaapo Kakko (6 G / 11 A / 17 P in 23 GP) isn’t far behind.
Devon Levi (10-4-0 / .889 SV% in 14 GS) will likely start for Edmonton, and Joey Daccord (6-5-0 / .881 SV% in 11 GS) for Seattle.
